Front: What are the stages from raw text to model input?
Back: Tokenization (text -> token strings) -> tensorization (token -> integer IDs, pad/truncate to uniform length, build attention mask) -> embeddings (IDs -> dense vectors, shape [batch, seq_len, embed_dim]).

Front: Why did NLP move to subword tokenization (BPE/WordPiece)?
Back: Solves out-of-vocabulary AND caps vocabulary size. Any word decomposes into known pieces (down to characters), so rare/new/misspelled words avoid a lossy [UNK] token.

Front: What does nn.Embedding store and do?
Back: A learnable lookup table of shape [vocab_size, embedding_dim]. A token ID returns (indexes) its row. Weights are learned (or init from pretrained). Relational geometry (king - man + woman ~= queen) is the real property; dimensions are not individually labeled.

Embedding = lookup only, returns per-token vectors [batch, seq_len, dim]. EmbeddingBag = lookup + pooling (mean/sum/max) fused, returns one vector per sequence [batch, dim], more efficient, handles variable length via offsets (no padding/mask).

Front: Why use EmbeddingBag for a simple text classifier?
Back: Bag-of-embeddings: represent text as the mean of its word vectors, then one Linear layer. EmbeddingBag does lookup+mean in one step, skips the big intermediate tensor, and handles variable lengths via offsets without padding.

Front: What does cosine similarity measure and why prefer it over Euclidean for embeddings?
Back: Cosine of the angle between vectors: +1 same direction, 0 unrelated, -1 opposite. Preferred because it ignores magnitude (often incidental, e.g. frequency); direction carries meaning. L2-normalize and Euclidean agrees with cosine.

Front: Why do padded batches need an attention mask?
Back: Padding adds fake filler tokens (id 0) to square the batch. The mask (1=real, 0=pad) makes the model ignore pad positions (-inf before softmax in attention; excluded from pooling). Without it, padding corrupts the output.

Front: How does nn.EmbeddingBag avoid the padding/mask problem?
Back: It uses offsets, not padding: a flat concatenation of all sequences plus an offsets tensor marking each start. Each bag pools only its own real tokens, so no pad tokens and no mask are needed.

Front: Fine-tuning BERT/DistilBERT: what do you keep vs add?
Back: Keep the pretrained transformer encoder + embeddings. Add a new classification head (Linear) on the [CLS]/pooled output for your labels. Full fine-tune (unfreeze whole encoder, small LR ~2e-5) is the common strong recipe; freeze-encoder + train-head is the lighter option.

Front: What produces DistilBERT and what is the trade-off?
Back: Knowledge distillation: a small student mimics a large teacher's output probabilities. ~40% smaller, ~60% faster, keeps ~97% of BERT's performance. Trade-off: small accuracy drop for a big size/speed win.

Front: Why is using one model's tokenizer with another model's weights a bug?
Back: Each tokenizer has its own vocab and ID->token mapping. Since embeddings are indexed by ID, mismatched IDs point to the wrong embedding rows, scrambling the input. Pair tokenizer + weights from the same checkpoint.

Front: Main caveat when reading a t-SNE plot?
Back: It preserves local neighborhoods only, so cluster sizes, gaps, and between-cluster distances are NOT meaningful. It is stochastic (runs differ) and sensitive to perplexity. PCA is the linear, variance-preserving alternative.
